+# Date Time Field
+
+<Subtitle>An easily stylable date time field component.</Subtitle>
+
+<Meta
+  name="description"
+  content="A high-quality, unstyled React date time field that is easy to customize."
+/>
+
+import { DemoDateTimeFieldHero } from './demos/hero';
+
+<DemoDateTimeFieldHero />
+
+## Usage guidelines
+
+- **Form controls must have an accessible name**: It can be created using a `<label>` element or the `Field` component. See the [forms guide](/react/handbook/forms).
+
+## Anatomy
+
+Import the component and assemble its parts:
+
+```jsx title="Anatomy"
+import { DateTimeField } from '@base-ui/react/date-time-field';
+
+<DateTimeField.Root>
+  <DateTimeField.SectionList>
+    {(section) => <DateTimeField.Section section={section} />}
+  </DateTimeField.SectionList>
+  <DateTimeField.Clear />
+</DateTimeField.Root>;
+```
+
+## API reference
+
+<Reference component="DateTimeField" parts="Root" />
+<Reference component="DateField" parts="Section, SectionList, Clear" />


body:
Have you considered extracting at least some types to a shared type?
Looks like there are multiple fields, which could reuse the same JSDoc across context, state, props, and calendar.

Nitpick: we no longer have test coverage analysis.
But I don't see a problem keeping this comment if it is ever brought back.
Nitpick: Have you considered calling these `TemporalField<stuff>` and aliasing everywhere to maintain consistency?

I don't have benchmarks on real app, but yes it decreases time spent on date manipulation significantly.
Even with a single field, we had computations on every render that were stable and could be cached.

I have a similar approach on the Scheduler.

@atomiks @colmtuite any preference?
Both are fine for me

It's already a standalone function though
If we use it in other components I can extract it in a different file.
I cannot be a constant since it's adapter dependant
I followed what we currently do for components like `Menu` (vs `ContextMenu`) but that's debatable
Considering this is only used in `packages/react/src/date-field/utils/TemporalFieldStore.ts`, could we keep this file in that local utils folder? It would avoid making it part of the public API.

I'm using it in the Scheduler + Tree View (on MUI X) and on the Tree PR on Base UI.
I neeed an equivalent of `useTimeout` for components with large stores out of React.
What problem do you see putting it in `@base-ui/utils`?
Good points. Probably not worth it making functions for building commonly used formats.

Gotcha.
Well, I don't see any clear issues with this approach; it should work nicely and improve performance. 👍

No objections to following that pattern.
I was just thinking from an ideological PoV, having a "base" (common) component that is aliased throughout all the usages could make sense. 🤔

I do agree that it could make sense
One could say that `ContextMenu` is derived from `Menu` which is the main component.
Whereas here `TimeField` is not less "main" than `DateField`
Exactly, that was my reasoning "in the head". 😆

The interval methods are only used on the Scheduler.
I can drop them in favor of an `IntervalManager` that I don't move to `@base-ui/utils` until it's used in 2-3 packages (why might never be the case).

The main downside I see with standalone timeouts is the cleanup, it's easy to miss one in the `mountEffect` cleanup function, especially with plugins.
But if you have a way to make them autoclean, I'm all in favor of removing the abstraction.

I'll fix the casing :+1:

Might be worth at least adding the `submitter` relationship as noted here:
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLFormElement/requestSubmit#examples
Yeah, from what I remember, we've gone with this approach on X Pickers for this exact edge-case reason of force-submitting without a submit button.
